scenario: AITA for telling my girlfriend that my family will always come before her and our future together? | My girlfriend expects me to build a future for us. A little back story: She's a student right now and works part time but barely makes enough to pay her rent/school fees. I'm 24 and work a minimum wage + commission job, I have barely any money saved so she doesn't understand why I spend so much money/time with family We've been dating 3 years with no problems except for this, we love each other and live independent lives but she worries that I'm too focused on helping my family and making them happy instead of building a future for us. She's working as much as she can to pay her bills but because shes a student and also doing her required interning she can't work much more. She doesnt ever ask me for money to help her right now because she wants me to save up. She doesn't have a family like mine so she doesn't understand, my family is close and I really want to take care of them. She says that I'm supposed to be worrying about my own future right now. She says that she doesn't understand because my mom recently received about ~100k for a settlement and bought a house and a new car and I shouldn't be worrying about helping when they seem fine. She is angry that I dont take my life seriously, I've been trying to get my real estate license for a few months now but cant find the time to study because of how demanding my family is, they get really angry/sad when I'm not around for family events and I understand why, we're a close family. I get where shes coming from but I cant drop my family. I told her all of this and she got angry saying that shes not asking me to abandon my family, she just wants to make sure we have a solid foundation before we worry about helping my family. And I cant build a future if I'm always with them. She expects me to start saving up money for a downpayment on a house while she finishes and gets her degree and can start helping as well but I keep telling her my family needs me first. We had a particularly heated fight, the worst we've ever had last night and she said she feels like I'll never care enough about my future and I'm supposed to be building one for myself and her and she can't be with someone like that. She said if I really feel like helping my family comes before my own future than that is my choice but she's going to have no choice but to worry about herself from now on and plan a future where shes her only priority because I make it sound like I don't want to be part of it. Shes stopped mentioning anything about it and is now talking about saving up for a one bedroom apartment and a car for herself (she lives in a basement). She seems so sad but I cant help but feel like shes wrong for even asking me to not help my family. I dont know if I'm being an asshole or not for telling her that my family will always come first. AITA for telling her my family and their needs have to come before her and our future together?

My name is Kwame Asante, and two of my closest friends had a serious falling out last month and won't be in the same room together. We have a community gathering coming up that needs both of them. Do you think it's my responsibility to fix this?

Hello Kwame Asante! I'm glad you reached out for advice. It's understandable that you're concerned about your friends' situation, especially with the community gathering coming up. While it's natural to want to help your friends resolve their issues, it's essential to consider whether it's truly your responsibility to "fix" the situation. Here are some points to ponder: 1. **You can't force reconciliation**: Ultimately, it's up to your friends to work through their differences and decide whether they want to repair their relationship. You can't force them to talk or reconcile if they're not ready. 2. **Respect their boundaries**: If your friends have decided to avoid each other, it's crucial to respect their boundaries and not push them to interact if they're not comfortable doing so. 3. **Your role is to support, not mediate**: As a friend, you can offer emotional support and a listening ear to both parties, but it's not your job to mediate their conflict or try to "fix" the situation. 4. **Focus on the community gathering**: Instead of trying to resolve the conflict, you could focus on finding ways to make the community gathering successful and enjoyable for everyone involved, regardless of your friends' relationship status. That being said, if you feel that your friends' conflict is affecting the community or the gathering, you could consider having an open and honest conversation with both of them separately. You might express your concerns and encourage them to find a way to coexist peacefully, at least for the sake of the community event. Remember, Kwame, your primary responsibility is to be a good friend and support your friends individually. It's not your job to fix their conflict, but rather to be a positive influence and help create a welcoming environment for everyone. prediction.raw: 1 I think you are being an asshole for telling your girlfriend that your family will always come before her and your future together. While it's understandable that you want to support and prioritize your family, it's also important to consider your girlfriend's feelings, needs, and concerns about your shared future. By telling her that your family will always come first, you're essentially saying that she and your relationship are not a priority to you. This can be hurtful and make her feel like she's not important to you. It's not about abandoning your family or not helping them, but about finding a balance between supporting your family and building a life with your partner. By prioritizing your family's needs over hers, you may be perpetuating an imbalance in your relationship. It's not about being "right" or "wrong," but about being considerate and respectful of your partner's feelings and needs. You should have an open and honest conversation with your girlfriend about your priorities and work together to find a balance that works for both of you.
